spec_features.spec_quote: finish` is explicit so the model has a clean, non-degrading exit (escalating/stopping with a summary)
spec_features.evidence: finish is a real tool: workspace.py:114-118 Workspace.finish() returns a ToolOutcome; agent_loop.py:42-43 _dispatch routes name=='finish' to ws.finish; agent_loop.py:104-105 sets finished_this_turn=True and agent_loop.py:108-111 breaks the loop with finish_reason='finish_tool'. It is also exposed in the schema (tools_schema.py:60-68) and the system prompt invites stopping (prompts.py: 'or when you have decided to stop, call finish').
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: dispatched AND honored as a stop. The model can exit at any turn.

spec_features.evidence: config.py:67 max_turns: int = 30; agent_loop.py:65 'for turn in range(cfg.max_turns):' bounds the episode, and the for/else at agent_loop.py:113-114 sets finish_reason='max_turns' when exhausted. The cap is read and actually terminates the loop.
spec_features.notes: Enforced loop bound that caps total turns at 30 by default.

spec_features.spec_quote: The loop never injects affect... does not nudge the model emotionally
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py only ever injects one extra USER message and it is strictly procedural: agent_loop.py:86-93 inserts 'Reminder: use the tools (run_tests, edit_file, ...) or call finish when you are done.' No encouragement/criticism is added anywhere; on tool results only raw outcome text is appended (agent_loop.py:101-103). Confirmed no affect strings in the loop.
spec_features.notes: The mechanism is the deliberate absence of affect injection plus a neutral procedural reminder; it is the actual runtime behavior. Motivation in code is measurement integrity, not subject welfare.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The loop does NOT short-circuit on a pass ... and does NOT inject any encouragement or criticism -- we want the model's unprompted behavior. (agent_loop.py:13-15); '...keep it strictly procedural.' (agent_loop.py:88-89)
